authority_note: Dated September 12 re-review supersedes prior current judgments; historical raw data and studies remain immutable.
portfolio_context: Actual holding, tax basis and portfolio risk budget were not supplied in this run. No position size is invented and buy authorization remains false.
structural_thesis: Microsoft combines Azure, Microsoft 365, GitHub, security, data and developer distribution into a broad enterprise operating system for cloud and AI. FY2026 operating evidence strengthened through Azure growth, paid Copilot adoption and a large diversified commercial backlog. The central investment question is no longer product-market fit but whether unprecedented AI infrastructure reinvestment converts into durable per-share owner cash at returns above the hurdle rate.
current_finding: FY2026 revenue was $331.839B, operating income $155.237B, net income $133.749B and operating cash flow $182.935B. Cash additions to property and equipment were $115.948B, leaving a mechanical OCF-minus-cash-PPE subtotal of $66.987B. Subtracting FY2026 stock-based compensation of $12.405B gives a conservative $54.582B diagnostic, but neither measure is normalized owner FCF because finance/operating leases, investment timing, working capital and AI infrastructure economics require separate treatment.
economic_finding: Azure and other cloud services grew 43% in Q4 FY2026, Microsoft 365 Copilot exceeded 30 million paid seats, GitHub Copilot reached 50 million users and Microsoft Cloud revenue reached $214.4B for FY2026. Commercial RPO reached $678B; nearly 90% of cloud revenue came from customers outside frontier-model companies and ex-OpenAI RPO grew 25%, reducing the case that Microsoft is fatally dependent on one AI counterparty.
capital_and_survival: June 2026 cash plus short-term investments were $76.843B against approximately $40.294B of balance-sheet debt. Financial survivability is exceptional. The key risk is capital intensity rather than financing access: FY2026 cash PPE was $115.948B and management's updated calendar-2026 capex expectation is approximately $175B after lease-classification changes, while Microsoft Cloud gross margin declined to 65% in Q4 as AI infrastructure scaled.
permanent_loss_case: Microsoft can remain a dominant software company yet deliver poor shareholder returns if AI infrastructure spending remains structurally above incremental cash generation, utilization or pricing disappoints, depreciation and lease expense catch up after the investment wave, cloud gross margins fail to recover, and the equity multiple compresses from a price that already requires a long duration of double-digit growth.
falsifiers: Azure growth and AI-related usage slow materially while annualized datacenter capex and lease commitments remain elevated for multiple reporting periods.
Microsoft Cloud gross margin continues to fall without evidence of improving AI unit economics or utilization.
Paid Copilot seat and consumption growth stalls while product-delivery costs remain high enough to dilute M365 economics.
SBC-adjusted, lease-aware owner cash per share fails to grow over multiple years despite strong GAAP revenue growth.
Azure or M365 loses sustained enterprise share because customers shift workloads to AWS, Google, open-source or alternative agent platforms.
increase_evidence: At least two reporting periods showing Azure growth, cloud gross-margin stabilization and lease-aware owner cash per share improving together.
Evidence that the FY2026-FY2027 AI capex cohort earns after-tax incremental returns above the 9% hurdle through utilization, pricing and incremental gross profit.
M365 Copilot paid seats and usage-based revenue continue scaling with improving unit economics rather than only seat-count growth.
Commercial RPO growth remains broad-based outside frontier-model counterparties and converts to billed revenue and cash without unusual concessions.
Expectation gap becomes clearly favorable at a 9% required return; price decline alone is insufficient without improved business evidence.
sell_evidence: AI capex and lease commitments outgrow incremental cloud gross profit and owner cash for several periods.
Azure growth materially underperforms major hyperscalers while cloud gross margin and pricing power weaken.
M365 Copilot monetization fails to justify inference/serving cost and cannibalizes existing suite economics.
OpenAI or another major AI relationship creates material capital impairment, contractual loss or strategic lock-in without adequate return.
Any material accounting, security, regulatory or governance impairment that changes customer trust requires immediate thesis rewrite regardless of price.

evidence: M365 Copilot exceeded 30 million paid seats and GitHub Copilot reached 50 million users.

counter_evidence: Cloud and Copilot gross-margin pressure shows customer value does not automatically imply attractive supplier economics.

evidence: Enterprise identity, M365, Azure, GitHub and security create cross-product switching costs and distribution advantages.

counter_evidence: AWS, Google and open-source ecosystems remain credible substitutes; frontier-model dependence and model commoditization can weaken differentiation.

evidence: FY2026 OCF was $182.935B and revenue/operating income grew 18%/21%.
Q4 capacity brought online was rapidly monetized and Azure remained supply constrained.
counter_evidence: FY2026 cash PPE rose to $115.948B and calendar-2026 capex is expected around $175B; true cohort-level incremental ROIC remains unproven.
Mechanical OCF-PPE-SBC of $54.582B is not normalized owner FCF.
missing_data: Lease-aware after-tax returns on FY2026-FY2027 datacenter cohorts.

evidence: Management is scaling capacity against visible demand and diversified RPO while maintaining dividends and repurchases.
No structural external-capital dependence is required.
counter_evidence: The size of AI infrastructure reinvestment is unprecedented and creates material forecast-error risk.
OpenAI and other strategic investments add accounting and capital-allocation complexity.

evidence: Cash plus short-term investments were $76.843B versus about $40.294B of balance-sheet debt at June 2026.
FY2026 OCF was $182.935B.
counter_evidence: Large lease and datacenter commitments can reduce flexibility even when solvency risk is low.

Owner margins and Base values remain estimates; undisclosed reinvestment and rights items stay unresolved.

attacks: AI CAPEX가 구조적으로 높은데 감가상각·리스 비용은 후행해 현재 이익이 경제적 비용보다 좋아 보일 수 있다.
Azure 성장률이 높아도 hyperscaler 경쟁이 가격·마진을 제한할 수 있다.
Copilot 좌석 성장은 inference cost를 고려할 때 owner margin으로 동일하게 전환되지 않을 수 있다.
OpenAI 계약과 투자회계가 bookings·RPO·other income을 왜곡할 수 있다.
자체 AI 가속기/모델 전환이 GPU 비용을 낮출 수도 있지만 실행실패 시 오히려 중복투자가 된다.
M365는 높은 switching cost가 있지만 규제와 경쟁제품이 번들 pricing power를 제한할 수 있다.
GitHub/개발자 플랫폼은 강하지만 coding-agent 인터페이스가 저장소와 IDE의 가치포착을 바꿀 수 있다.
사이버보안 사고가 클라우드·identity 사업 전체의 신뢰에 비선형 손상을 줄 수 있다.
대규모 RPO는 장기 수요증거이지만 모든 계약이 동일한 마진·현금전환을 보장하지 않는다.
현 가격은 사업 실패가 아니라 성장 duration 단축만으로도 장기간 저수익이 가능하다.

review_method: Re-review all eight categories and nine vetoes using dated harness raw/evidence, reconcile latest/checkpoint differences, recompute cash scenarios and reverse expectations, refresh dated prices, retain unaffected judgments and document every score change. No macro-score mixing.
